evidence.title: McIntosh County Commissioners extend road moratorium on wind and solar projects
evidence.supports: Confirms the McIntosh County Board voted 'Monday, June 1' to extend the July 2025 county-road-use moratorium on wind/solar construction traffic, but the article (checked against a full re-fetch and the syndicated Eufaula Indian Journal copy) does not state the length or new end date of the extension.
evidence.quote: The McIntosh County Board of County Commissioners voted Monday, June 1, to extend its moratorium on the use of county-maintained roads for the transport and delivery of equipment and materials associated with the construction of wind turbines, solar panels, and related infrastructure.

evidence.title: McIntosh County Proceedings, June 3, 2026 (Board of Equalization / Regular Meeting)
evidence.supports: The county's own posted minutes for its closest listed meeting to the reported June 1 vote (June 3, 2026, the only regular meeting between May 13 and July 8, 2026) contain no mention of a road-use moratorium, wind, solar, or an extension vote, so the endpoint could not be corroborated from official minutes.
evidence.quote: Next meeting will be July 8, 2026... There being no further business... Meeting adjourned.

evidence.title: Wind energy benefits North Dakota. So why has the state soured on it?
evidence.supports: Independently describes a McIntosh County wind-project moratorium adopted 'in April' 2026 ('a few months after Badger Wind Farm went online' in January 2026), described as a one-year moratorium on siting new wind projects -- a different description (substantive siting pause, April 2026) than this row's July-2025 road-haul-traffic restriction.
evidence.quote: in April — a few months after Badger Wind Farm went online — McIntosh County adopted a one-year moratorium on new wind projects, citing concerns about how another Ørsted project, proposed for the south part of the county, would impact nonparticipant property owners.

decisions.notes: EXTENDED_NO_END_DATE not resolved: confirmed (via two independently published copies of the same wire story, McIntosh Democrat and Eufaula Indian Journal) that the Board voted to extend the road-use moratorium on 'Monday, June 1' [2026], but neither copy states the new term length or end date, and both cut off at the same point (likely the full extent of a short local-paper item, not a paywall truncation -- re-fetched with --refresh and confirmed identical). Checked the county's own posted meeting-minutes archive (olivercountynd.org-style county-proceedings page) and pulled the full text of the closest listed meeting, the June 3, 2026 Regular Meeting/Board of Equalization minutes (all 4 pages, via direct PDF download) -- it contains no mention of the road-use moratorium, wind, or solar at all, and June 1, 2026 (a Monday) does not correspond to any meeting on the county's own list of Regular/Special Meetings (which runs May 13 -> June 3 -> July 8), so the vote may have occurred at an unlisted committee/special session, or the article's date may be imprecise. Leaving the record as-is (extended, no end date) rather than guessing. Separately noted for the coordinator: a Canary Media investigative piece (Sept. 2026) describes a distinct-sounding McIntosh County 'one-year moratorium on new wind projects' adopted in April 2026 over siting concerns for a second Ørsted wind project -- this reads as a different, more substantive land-use/siting moratorium than the row's July-2025 road-haul-traffic restriction, and may be a missing instrument, but this QA4 pass does not add new_candidates; flagging for a future full-research pass.

legal_basis.to: Resolution 2025-02, 'A Resolution of the County of Oliver, North Dakota, to Impose a Moratorium on the Development of All Data Center and Cryptocurrency Mining Facilities Until Zoning Standards Can Be Developed' (companion to Resolution 2025-03, the separate Solar Energy Facilities moratorium); second reading and adoption at the May 6, 2025 Commission meeting; vote 2-1, Berger and Schmidt aye, Husfloen nay, per official minutes
legal_basis.reason: The county's own posted minutes for the April 15, 2025 Planning & Zoning first reading and the May 6, 2025 Commission second reading/adoption both show Resolution 2025-02 is titled the Data Center AND Cryptocurrency Mining Facilities moratorium, while Resolution 2025-03 is titled the separate Solar Energy Facilities moratorium. The row's own jurisdiction label is '(Phase 2)' data center track with sectors=["data_center"], so its legal_basis should cite 2025-02, not 2025-03 (which is the solar instrument the SECTOR_CHECK flag is asking about).

sectors.reason: Resolution 2025-02's own text (the corrected legal_basis) imposes the moratorium on 'all data centers AND cryptocurrency mining facilities' as a single combined instrument -- the same pattern used elsewhere in this inventory for Oliver County Phase 1 and Phase 3. Cryptocurrency mining is operative scope of this resolution, not a trigger mention or a separate instrument.

evidence.title: Oliver County Commission Proceedings, May 6, 2025

decisions.notes: SECTOR_CHECK resolved: the 'solar' mention in the row's own duration/legal_basis text refers to Resolution 2025-03, a separate, distinctly numbered solar-only instrument adopted the same day -- a companion instrument, not this row's operative scope -- so solar correctly stays out of sectors. While confirming that, found and fixed two adjacent errors surfaced by reading the same primary minutes: legal_basis had the wrong resolution number for the data-center instrument (2025-03 instead of 2025-02, i.e. it was citing the solar resolution's number), and that correctly-cited resolution 2025-02 turns out to also cover cryptocurrency mining facilities (title: 'Data Center and Cryptocurrency Mining Facilities'), so cryptocurrency_mining was added to sectors.

sectors.reason: Oliver County's own March 13, 2026 Commission minutes describe the second reading and adoption of 'Resolution 2026-02 for Data Center and Cryptocurrency Mining Facilities moratorium' as a single combined instrument, consistent with the row's own legal_basis text ('a 180-day moratorium on data center and cryptocurrency mining facilities'). This is operative scope stated in the resolution's own title/adoption language, not a trigger mention or a separate instrument.
